title: Closed exceptional comparison under site comparison
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell
e p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\ge1$. Put $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] of separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with complementary open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow T$ [def-weil-open-immersion]. Work in the ordinary derived categories of constant-$A$ module sheaves on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], with comparison morphisms $
u_W:W_{\mathrm{proet}}	o W_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. For $	au=\mathrm{et},\mathrm{proet}$ let $I_	au=Ri_	au^!$ be the ambient right adjoint to closed direct image $i_{	au,*}$ [lem-exc-closed-ambient, lem-exc-proetale-closed-support], with counit $\epsilon^	au$.

For every $M\in D^b_c(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes], $I_{\mathrm{et}}M$ is bounded below. For bounded-below etale $L$ on $Z$, let $\delta_L:
u_T^*i_{\mathrm{et},*}L\xrightarrow{\sim}i_{\mathrm{proet},*}
u_Z^*L$ be the canonical direct-image comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate]. Define $\alpha_M$ as the $i_{\mathrm{proet},*}\dashv I_{\mathrm{proet}}$ transpose of $
u_T^*(\epsilon^{\mathrm{et}}_M)\circ\delta_{I_{\mathrm{et}}M}^{-1}$. Then
$$\alpha_M:
u_Z^*I_{\mathrm{et}}M\xrightarrow{\sim}I_{\mathrm{proet}}
u_T^*M$$
is an isomorphism, natural in $M$, and
$$\epsilon^{\mathrm{proet}}_{
u_T^*M}\circ i_{\mathrm{proet},*}(\alpha_M)\circ\delta_{I_{\mathrm{et}}M}=
u_T^*(\epsilon^{\mathrm{et}}_M).$$

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: compare the closed-support triangles

proof.text: Write $F_W=\nu_W^*$. The ring $A$ is finite and commutative. The spectrum of the field $k$ is Noetherian: its only ideals are $0,k$ and its spectrum has one point. Thus $T,Z$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. The open $U$ is Noetherian, hence quasi-compact, by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. The schemes are separated over $k$ (and $U$ is an open of the separated scheme $T$), so they are quasi-separated. By [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], both $i$ and $j$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated. This verifies the hypotheses of the pro-etale closed-support results and of the canonical direct-image comparison for both immersions.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: compare the closed-support triangles

proof.text: First check the boundedness needed to define $\delta_{I_{\mathrm{et}}M}$. The etale support triangle of [lem-exc-closed-support-triangle] gives $i_{\mathrm{et},*}I_{\mathrm{et}}M\to M\to Rj_{\mathrm{et},*}j_{\mathrm{et}}^*M\to$. Exact etale module inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] preserves bounded below objects: exactness identifies kernels and images and thus commutes with cohomology. Since $M$ is bounded, $j_{\mathrm{et}}^*M$ is bounded below; its derived direct image is bounded below by [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Closure of $D^+$ under triangles [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories] shows that $i_{\mathrm{et},*}I_{\mathrm{et}}M$ is bounded below. By [lem-kun-04ca], $i_{\mathrm{et}}^*i_{\mathrm{et},*}\cong\mathrm{id}$ on abelian sheaves. This isomorphism respects constant $A$-actions, since it is natural with respect to multiplication by each scalar; therefore it holds on module sheaves and termwise on complexes. The direct image in the support triangle is termwise; applying the exact $i_{\mathrm{et}}^*$ gives $I_{\mathrm{et}}M$ bounded below. In particular the isomorphism $\delta_{I_{\mathrm{et}}M}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate] is defined. No constructibility of $I_{\mathrm{et}}M$ has been used.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: compare the closed-support triangles

proof.text: On pro-etale module sheaves $i_{\mathrm{proet},*}$ is exact by [lem-exc-proetale-closed-exact], and its ordinary inverse-image counit $i_{\mathrm{proet}}^*i_{\mathrm{proet},*}\to\mathrm{id}$ is an isomorphism by [lem-exc-proetale-closed-fully-faithful]. The inverse image is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact]. The module adjunction $i_{\mathrm{proet}}^*\dashv i_{\mathrm{proet},*}$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] consequently descends termwise to the ordinary derived categories: apply localization to its termwise unit and counit; their two triangle identities still hold. Its counit is still invertible. Hence closed direct image is fully faithful there: its adjunction bijection identifies maps $i_*P\to i_*Q$ with maps $i^*i_*P\to Q$, and composing with the inverse-image counit identifies the latter with maps $P\to Q$. It reflects isomorphisms, since fullness lifts an inverse and faithfulness verifies its two inverse identities.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: compare the closed-support triangles

proof.text:
Let $a=a_j:F_Uj_{\mathrm{et}}^*\xrightarrow{\sim}j_{\mathrm{proet}}^*F_T$ be [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback], and let $b=b_j$ be [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate]. Set
$$\gamma_M=Rj_{\mathrm{proet},*}(a_M)\circ b_{j,j_{\mathrm{et}}^*M}:F_TRj_{\mathrm{et},*}j_{\mathrm{et}}^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}Rj_{\mathrm{proet},*}j_{\mathrm{proet}}^*F_TM.$$
All inputs to $b$ are bounded below by Step 2. We verify the unit square, rather than choosing an unspecified isomorphism. Write $\eta^e,\eta^p$ for the open-adjunction units and $\varepsilon^e$ for the etale open counit. Under $j_{\mathrm{proet}}^*\dashv Rj_{\mathrm{proet},*}$ the transpose of $b_{j,j_{\mathrm{et}}^*M}\circ F_T(\eta^e_M)$ is, by the defining mate formula,
$$F_U(\varepsilon^e_{j_{\mathrm{et}}^*M})\circ a_{Rj_{\mathrm{et},*}j_{\mathrm{et}}^*M}^{-1}\circ j_{\mathrm{proet}}^*F_T(\eta^e_M)
=F_U(\varepsilon^e_{j_{\mathrm{et}}^*M}\circ j_{\mathrm{et}}^*\eta^e_M)\circ a_M^{-1}=a_M^{-1}.$$
The first equality is naturality of $a$, the second the adjunction triangle identity. Applying $a_M$ proves $\gamma_M\circ F_T(\eta^e_M)=\eta^p_{F_TM}$.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: compare the closed-support triangles

proof.text:
The exact functor $F_T$ of [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact] carries distinguished triangles to distinguished triangles by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. Apply it to the etale support triangle [lem-exc-closed-support-triangle] and identify its first term using $\delta_{I_{\mathrm{et}}M}$. Its first arrow is then
$$u_M=F_T(\epsilon^{\mathrm{et}}_M)\circ\delta_{I_{\mathrm{et}}M}^{-1}:i_{\mathrm{proet},*}F_ZI_{\mathrm{et}}M\to F_TM.$$
Compare with the pro-etale support triangle [lem-exc-proetale-support-triangle] at $F_TM$. Its first arrow is the exceptional counit and its second the open unit: these normalizations are explicitly given by [lem-exc-proetale-derived-adjunction-triangle] and [lem-exc-proetale-open-derived-image], using their common K-injective representative. The hypotheses of the derived-adjunction statement hold by Step 3, the restriction description in the open-derived-image statement, and [lem-exc-proetale-closed-essential-image]: closed images have zero open restriction and every sheaf with zero open restriction has invertible closed unit. Identify its derived right adjoint with $I_{\mathrm{proet}}$ by the unique right-adjoint isomorphism preserving the counit. Step 4 gives the commuting square between the second arrows with vertical maps $1_{F_TM}$ and $\gamma_M$. Rotate both triangles and apply TR3 in [def-weil-triangulated-category], then rotate back. This supplies a first vertical map
$$f_M:i_{\mathrm{proet},*}F_ZI_{\mathrm{et}}M\longrightarrow i_{\mathrm{proet},*}I_{\mathrm{proet}}F_TM$$
with $\epsilon^{\mathrm{proet}}_{F_TM}\circ f_M=u_M$. Since the other two vertical maps are isomorphisms, [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] makes $f_M$ an isomorphism.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: compare the closed-support triangles

proof.text: By the derived full faithfulness in Step 3, $f_M=i_{\mathrm{proet},*}(\beta_M)$ for a unique map $\beta_M:F_ZI_{\mathrm{et}}M\to I_{\mathrm{proet}}F_TM$. The equation from Step 5 says $\epsilon^{\mathrm{proet}}_{F_TM}\circ i_{\mathrm{proet},*}(\beta_M)=u_M$. Under the exceptional adjunction [lem-exc-proetale-closed-support], this is exactly the statement that $\beta_M$ is the transpose of $u_M$, hence $\beta_M=\alpha_M$ as defined in the item. Since $i_{\mathrm{proet},*}$ reflects isomorphisms, $\alpha_M$ is invertible. Multiplying this equation on the right by $\delta_{I_{\mathrm{et}}M}$ gives the required counit identity. Finally $u_M$ is natural, because $\delta$ is natural by [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate] and $\epsilon^{\mathrm{et}}$ is the adjunction counit [lem-exc-closed-ambient]. For $h:M\to N$, naturality of $u$ and of the pro-etale counit shows that the two maps $I_{\mathrm{proet}}F_T(h)\circ\alpha_M$ and $\alpha_N\circ F_ZI_{\mathrm{et}}(h)$ have the same transpose $F_T(h)\circ u_M=u_N\circ i_{\mathrm{proet},*}F_ZI_{\mathrm{et}}(h)$. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection makes them equal. Thus the specified isomorphism is natural; no natural choice of the TR3 completion is required.
